"108 :     @Deprecated
109 :     public void addValue(Object v) {
110 :             addValue((Comparable<?>) v);            
111 :     }"

messages.name: get_code_snippet

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The test case testAddNonComparable is designed to verify that adding a non-comparable Object to the Frequency instance should throw an IllegalArgumentException. The test calls f.addValue(new Object()) and expects an exception.

Looking at the implementation of Frequency.addValue(Object), the method is deprecated and simply casts the Object to Comparable and calls addValue(Comparable<?>). This cast does not perform a check to confirm if the Object implements Comparable; it just performs the cast, which means it could cause a ClassCastException at runtime if the Object does not implement Comparable.

In the Frequency.addValue(Comparable<?>) method, the passed Comparable v is internally used as an Object key in the freqTable map. The method tries to update the frequency count for the key, putting the object into freqTable. If the object is not Comparable (or at least not comparable to the objects already present), the TreeMap freqTable will throw a ClassCastException when trying to compare keys.

When this ClassCastException occurs, it is caught and wrapped as an IllegalArgumentException with message "Value not comparable to existing values."

Despite this, the original addValue(Object) method does not prohibit adding a plain Object. It merely casts and relies on the underlying TreeMap to detect incompatibility. Given that the first call to addValue(new Object()) in the test passes without exception (was "previously OK"), but the second call fails with an IllegalArgumentException indicates that the first call inserts a non-comparable object into the freqTable keys. On subsequent insertions, the TreeMap encounters comparison between heterogeneous keys, leading to ClassCastException.

The bug report complains that this behavior is undesirable. The addValue(Object) should not allow adding non-Comparable objects at all, preventing the inconsistent state of having mixed comparable and non-comparable keys in freqTable. Instead, there should be a stricter type check in addValue(Object), refusing to accept plain Object instances that do not implement Comparable.

Therefore, the root cause of the failure and API bug is that addValue(Object) improperly accepts any Object and relies on a cast to Comparable and TreeMap runtime exceptions to detect incompatibility, rather than actively rejecting non-comparable objects upfront. This allows invalid keys into freqTable, leading to failing additions on subsequent calls.

No relevant information is found in the recent bug reports as they address other unrelated issues.

Summary: The failing test exposes that addValue(Object) must check explicitly that the input implements Comparable rather than blindly casting. This prevents putting non-comparable keys into freqTable and the eventual IllegalArgumentException at later additions. The lack of this check is the cause of the bug and test failure.
org.apache.commons.math.stat.Frequency.addValue(java.lang.Object)
org.apache.commons.math.stat.Frequency.addValue(java.lang.Comparable<?>)
